title: DR1 lists the four things that can identify the means of transport as bullets; the frontend runs them together into one sentence separated by semicolons, with the list opener left mid-air as "enter (one of the following):".

finding.frontend: The hint under Transport identification is a single string: "To identify the means of transport, enter (one of the following): flight number; train number; road vehicle registration number; vessel name (for ferries, also the road vehicle registration number)" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:24-27). It wraps to three lines of grey text, and the four alternatives are separated only by semicolons, one of which sits next to a semicolon-free parenthetical. A user has already chosen their means of transport two questions earlier, so they are scanning that sentence for the one item that applies to them.
finding.prototype: DR1 uses the same words but sets them as a colon-ended opener followed by a bulleted list of four items — flight number, train number, road vehicle registration number, vessel name (for ferries, also the road vehicle registration number) (app/views/arrival-details.html:122-129). Each alternative is one line, and the one a user needs is found by looking rather than by parsing.
finding.difference: Split the hint into an opening sentence and a four-item bulleted list, keeping the wording as it is. The hint is currently a single copy string, so the field's hint has to accept markup or the list has to move into the template above the input.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding the frontend's transport-identification hint rendered as a list rather than a single paragraph — the captured page model records it as one hint string with the items run together.
finding.correction: VERIFIED SOUND. DR1 passes the hint as HTML — a colon-ended opening paragraph followed by a four-item govuk-list govuk-list--bullet (app/views/arrival-details.html:126-129) — and the captured dr1-arrival-details screenshot shows four bullets. The frontend's hint is a single string with semicolons (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/copy/copy.en.js:24-26) and the captured fe-arrival-details screenshot shows it wrapped over three lines of grey text. The wording is word-for-word identical on both sides, so this is purely how the hint is set, and the difference is right that the hint is a plain copy string today and so either has to accept markup or the list has to move into the template.
